en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Book of Puzzles,
Chapter on the Power of Supernatural Faculties.
6. The Question on Descent into the Womb “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, through the coming together of three things, there is descent into the womb; here, mother and father [come together].’”

‘And when these three things come together—there is the union of the parents, the mother is in her season, and the *gandhabba* is present—then, monks, through the coming together of these three, there is the descent into the womb.

This is a statement that is exhaustive, this is a statement that is complete, this is a statement that is non-figurative, this is a statement worthy of an *arhat*; it was spoken while sitting in the midst of gods and humans.
And this descent of an embryo is seen to result from the union of two factors:
when the ascetic Dukūla touched the navel of the female ascetic Pārikā with his right thumb at the time of her heat,
Prince Sāma was reborn because of that touching of the navel.
The seer Mātaṅga also touched the navel of a Brahmin girl with the tip of his right thumb at the time of her menses; by that touching of the navel, a young brahmin named Maṇḍabya was reborn.
If, venerable Nāgasena, it was said by the Blessed One:
“Monks, through the conjunction of three things, there is the descent into the womb.”
"In that case, the statement that both Prince Sāma and the young brahmin Maṇḍabya were reborn through the act of stroking the navel is false.
Venerable sir, if it was said by the Tathāgata,

‘Prince Sāma and the young brahmin Maṇḍabya were reborn through the act of stroking the navel,’ then the statement, ‘Monks, the descent into the womb occurs through the conjunction of three things,’ must also be false."
“This too is a question with two sides, profoundly deep and a subtle domain for the wise; it has come to you. Cut through the path of doubt and uphold the supreme radiance of knowledge.
“O Great King, this was indeed spoken by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, the descent of the embryo occurs through the conjunction of three things:
here, the mother and father must be united, the mother must be in her fertile season, and the *gandhabba* [must be present].’”
“And when these three things come together, there is the descent of the embryo.
And it has been said:
“The prince Sāma and the young brahmin Maṇḍabya were reborn through the act of touching the navel.”
“Therefore, venerable Nāgasena, by whatever means the question may be well-determined, by that means please convince me.
“But have you ever heard before, Great King, that the youth Saṅkicca, the ascetic Isisiṅga, and the elder Kumārakassapa were reborn from such [causes] as these?
“Yes, venerable sir, it has been heard; their births are well-known. Two deer-cows, during the heat of the season, [gave birth to two fawns]...”
Having come to the place where the ascetics discharged urine, they drank the urine along with its residue;
through that residue of urine, the youth Saṅkicca and the ascetic Isisiṅga were conceived.
When the elder Udāyin entered the nuns' quarters, as he gazed lustfully at the private parts of a nun, semen was emitted from his saffron robe.
Then the Venerable Udāyī said this to that bhikkhunī:
“Go, sister, bring some water; I will wash my inner robe.
“Bring it, venerable sir, I myself will wash it.”
“Then, at the time of her menses, that bhikkhunī took a portion of that conception with her mouth and placed another portion into her womb; thus, the Elder Kumārakassapa was born—so people say.
“But do you, Great King, believe that statement?
“Yes, venerable sir, we perceive a powerful reason for it, by which reason we believe he was born through that cause.”
“But what is the reason for this, Great King?
“Venerable sir, because a seed that has fallen upon well-prepared soil sprouts quickly.
“Yes, Great King,” [the Blessed One replied].

“In the same way, Bhante, that bhikkhunī, being in her season, when the embryo had coagulated and the blood’s flow had ceased, while the primary elements remained stable, she took that conception and placed it into that coagulated mass; by that means, her womb became established.
Thus we perceive the cause for their arising therein.”
“It is so, Great King; I accept it thus: that an embryo comes to be through entry into a womb.
But do you, Great King, accept the conception in the womb of the Elder Kumāra Kassapa?
“Yes, venerable sir,” he replied.
“Excellent, Great King! You have returned to my domain.

Even if you were to speak of the descent of the embryo in only one way, you would be supporting me; for do you believe in the descent of the embryo in those two milch-cows who, after drinking urine, conceived?”
“Yes, venerable sir, whatever has been eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted—all that flows into the *kalala* and, having reached its place, attains growth.
Just as, venerable Nāgasena, whatever rivers there may be, they all flow into the great ocean and, having reached their place, attain growth;
even so, venerable Nāgasena, whatever has been eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted—all that [flows into the *kalala*].”
“The *kalala* descends, and having reached its place, it attains growth; for that reason, I believe that even by what enters the mouth, there is the descent into the womb.
“Excellent, Great King! You have entered even more deeply into my domain; even by drinking through the mouth, there occurs the union of the two.”
“Great King, do you accept the descent into the womb of Prince Saṅkicca, of the ascetic Isisiṅga, of the elder Thera, and of Kumārakassapa?
“Yes, venerable sir, the convergence [of conditions] applies.
“Great King, Prince Sāma and the youth Maṇḍabya are also included within these three convergences; they are of the same essence as the former. I shall explain the reason for this.”

“Great King, both the ascetic Dukūla and the female ascetic Pārikā were dwellers in the forest, devoted to seclusion, and seekers of the supreme goal. By the power of their ascetic heat, they caused even the Brahma-world to glow.
At that time, Sakka, lord of the devas, used to come to attend upon them morning and evening.
Observing their profound affection for one another, he foresaw that in the future both of their eyes would perish. Having seen this, he spoke to them thus:”
“Sirs, do me this one favor: please have one son each; he will be your attendant and your support.
“Enough, Kosiya, do not speak thus,” they replied, and they did not accept his words.
Out of compassion and wishing for their welfare, Sakka, lord of the devas, said this to them a second time and a third time:
“Sirs, please do one thing for me; it would be well if you were each to have one son, who will become your attendant and your support.”
A third time they said to him: “Enough, Kosiya; do not involve us in what is disadvantageous.
When will this body not break up? Let this body break up, for it is subject to breaking up.
Even when the earth dissolves, when the mountain peaks collapse, and when the moon and sun fall from the sky, we shall never be mixed with worldly conditions.”
"Do not come into our presence; this confidence you have placed in one who has approached you is misplaced, for I think you are a doer of harm.
Then Sakka, Lord of the Devas, finding no favor in their minds, respectfully joined his palms and entreated them again:
"If you are unable to carry out my word, then when the female ascetic becomes fertile and menstruating, at that time you—"
“Venerable sir, you should touch her navel with the tip of your right thumb;
by that she will conceive, for this is the very conjunction required for the descent of the embryo.
“I am able to do as you say, Kosiya, but our asceticism is not broken by that much; let it be so.”
They accepted it.

Now, at that time, there was a son of the gods in the celestial realm who had accumulated abundant roots of merit; his lifespan was exhausted and he had reached the end of his life, yet he was capable of descending wherever he wished, even into the family of a universal monarch (cakkavatti).
Then Sakka, lord of the devas, approached that son of the gods and spoke thus:
"Come, dear sir! Your day has dawned auspiciously; the fulfillment of your purpose is at hand, for which I have come to attend upon you.
You shall dwell in a delightful place, you shall receive rebirth in a worthy family, and you shall be raised by beautiful parents.
Come, do as I say," he entreated.
A second time… and a third time,
he entreated him with his hands joined in reverence above his head.
Then that son of the gods spoke thus:
“Which family is that, dear sir, which you praise again and again? “The ascetic Dukūla and the female ascetic Pārikā.
Having heard his words, he was pleased and accepted them, saying, “Excellent, dear sir! Let it be as you wish.”

“If I so desire, dear sir, may I be reborn in a family of my choice; in what kind of family shall I be reborn—among those born from eggs, or from a womb, or from moisture, or by spontaneous generation?
“Be reborn, dear sir, from a womb,” he replied.
Then Sakka, Lord of the Devas, calculated the day of conception and informed the ascetic Dukkula:
"On such-and-such a day, the female ascetic will be in her season and menstruating; at that time, venerable sir, you should touch her navel with the thumb of your right hand."
On that day, Great King, the female ascetic was in her season and possessed of flowers; a son of the gods was present there;
and the male ascetic touched the female ascetic’s navel with the thumb of his right hand.
Thus, these three conditions came together. By that touching of the navel, passion arose in the female ascetic, and it [overwhelmed] her.
"Lust does not arise dependent upon embracing; do not think that only sexual intercourse is 'sannipāta' (convergence).

Laughter is also *sannipāta*, flattery is also *sannipāta*, and even contemplation is *sannipāta*. Because it is a preliminary stage for the arising of lust, convergence (*sannipāta*) occurs through touching; from such convergence, there is the descent into [sexual union]."
Even in the case of one who does not commit misconduct, Great King, conception occurs through physical contact.
Just as, Great King, a blazing fire dispels the cold of one who has approached it even without touching it,
even so, Great King, conception occurs through physical contact even in the case of one who does not commit misconduct.

"Great King, the descent of beings into the womb occurs by way of four factors: by way of karma, by way of the birthplace, by way of the family, and by way of prayer. Nevertheless, all these beings are born of karma and originate from karma.
How, Great King, does the descent of beings into the womb occur by way of karma?
Beings who have accumulated roots of merit, Great King, arise according to their wish in a great noble khattiya family, or..."
Whether in a great brahmin family, or a great householder family, or among the devas,
or by way of an egg-born birth, or a womb-born birth, or a moisture-born birth,
or a spontaneously born birth. Just as, Great King, a man might be wealthy, possessing great riches and vast enjoyments, with abundant gold and silver, and abundant means of livelihood.
Possessing abundant wealth and grain, and having a vast circle of kinsmen, he would purchase a female slave, a male slave, a field, a site,
a village, a town, or a district— whatever his heart desired— by paying double or even triple the price according to his wish.

In the same way, Great King, beings who have accumulated abundant roots of merit arise according to their wish in a great khattiya family, or a great brahmin family, or a great householder family; or among the devas;
or in an egg-born womb, or a womb-born womb, or a moisture-born womb, or a spontaneously born womb.
Thus is the descent of beings into the womb by way of karma.
How, Great King, is the descent of beings into the womb by way of the birth-place?
In the case of chickens, Great King, the descent into the womb occurs by means of the wind.
The entry into the womb of cranes occurs by the sound of thunderclouds.
All the deities are indeed beings who do not dwell in a womb; their entry into the womb occurs through various forms of manifestation.
Just as, Great King, humans move upon the earth in various ways—some concealing themselves in front, some...
They covered themselves from behind; some were naked, some were deformed yet wore white garments,
some had their hair tied in topknots, some were deformed yet wore saffron robes, some wore saffron robes with their hair in topknots,
some had matted hair and wore bark garments, some wore skins, and some wore horse-ribs as clothing— all of these were men.
They move upon the earth in various colors;
even so, Great King, all those beings are indeed beings, yet their descent into the womb occurs with various colors.
Thus does the descent of beings into the womb occur according to the mode of birth.
How, Great King, does the descent of beings into the womb occur by way of lineage?
Lineage, Great King, consists of four types: egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously born.
If, having come from anywhere, a *gandhabba* is reborn there in an egg-born lineage, he becomes egg-born therein... [and so on].
He is reborn in a family born from a lotus,
or in a family born from moisture,
or in a family of spontaneous birth; there, he is one of spontaneous birth.
In those various families, beings of a corresponding nature are reborn.
Just as, O Great King, whatever beasts or birds come to Mount Neru in the Himalayas, they all abandon their own natural colors and become golden-hued;
even so, O Great King, whatever gandhabba comes from wherever it may be and enters an egg-born womb, it abandons its inherent color and becomes an egg-born being... [and so forth].
Having entered the womb-born, moisture-born,
or spontaneously born mode of birth, one abandons one's natural color and becomes spontaneously born; such is the descent into the womb of beings according to their lineage.
How does the descent of beings into the womb occur by means of entreaty?

Here, Great King, there is a family that is childless, possessing great wealth, endowed with faith and confidence, virtuous, of noble character, and devoted to austerity; and there is a son of the gods who has accumulated abundant roots of merit and is subject to passing away.
Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, out of compassion for that family, entreats that son of the gods: "Make a resolution, dear sir, to enter the womb of the chief queen of such-and-such a family."
Thus, because of his entreaty, Sakka causes that deity to be directed toward that family.
Great King, just as people desiring merit, having entreated a venerable ascetic, bring him to their home with the thought, "He, having approached, will bring happiness to the entire family," even so,
Great King, does Sakka, lord of the devas, having entreated that deity, direct him toward that family.
Thus, through the power of a prayer, the descent of beings into the womb occurs.
Great King, Prince Sāma was requested by Sakka, the lord of the gods, and entered the womb of the ascetic woman Pārikā.

Great King, Prince Sāma had performed meritorious deeds; his parents were virtuous and of noble character; and the petitioner was Sakka. Through the convergence of these three mental aspirations, Prince Sāma was reborn.
“In this case, great king, suppose a man skilled in methods were to sow seed in a well-prepared, weed-free field; would there be any obstacle to the growth of that seed as it avoids all impediments?
“Certainly not, venerable sir; the undamaged seed would quickly sprout.
“In the same way, great king, Prince Sāma has escaped from obstacles and been reborn through the fulfillment of three mental aspirations.”
“Have you ever heard, Great King, that by the mental malice of seers (*isī*), a prosperous and flourishing great country, together with its people, was utterly destroyed?
“Yes, venerable sir, I have heard it.
The Daṇḍaka forest, the Majjha forest, the Kāliṅga forest, and the Mātaṅga forest—all those forests became mere wilderness; all those countries came to ruin through the mental malice of seers.”
“If, great king, by the mental corruption of those people their well-prosperous provinces were destroyed, would anything be produced by their mental serenity?
“Yes, venerable sir.
“In that case, great king, Prince Sāma was produced by the mental serenity of three powerful beings; he was fashioned by seers, fashioned by gods, and fashioned by merit.”
"Thus it is, great king; you should bear this in mind.
There are these three sons of gods, great king, who were born into families at the request of Sakka, lord of the devas.
Which three?"
“Prince Sāma, Mahāpanāda, and King Kusa—these too were Bodhisattvas.

“It has been well-explained, venerable Nāgasena; the descent into the womb has been clearly demonstrated. The reason has been well-stated; darkness has been turned into light; the tangle has been disentangled; the doctrines of opponents have been cleared away. It is so; thus do I accept it. The sixth chapter: The Question on the Descent into the Womb.
